name: Uric acid
rangeNote: Typical ranges: 3.5–7.2 mg/dL (208–428 µmol/L) for men and women after menopause, 2.6–6.0 mg/dL (155–357 µmol/L) for women before menopause. The app uses age 50 as a rough stand-in for menopause. Levels can rise after a large meal, alcohol or hard exercise.
summary: Uric acid (urate) is a waste product made when the body breaks down purines, substances found in its own cells and in many foods. The kidneys remove most of it.

high.meaning: A high uric acid can form crystals in joints (gout) or kidney stones, though many people with a high level never develop either. Studies also link high uric acid with heart and kidney disease, but they have not shown that uric acid itself causes these.
commonCauses: Water pills (diuretics) and some other medicines
Foods rich in purines, such as red meat, organ meats and some seafood

low.meaning: A low uric acid rarely causes problems by itself. It most often comes from medicines that lower it.
commonCauses: Medicines that lower uric acid, such as those used for gout
Some other medicines, such as SGLT2 inhibitor diabetes medicines
Rare inherited kidney or enzyme conditions
